text:
A 7-1 score suggests a rout from the opening faceoff, but the first period was closer than that. NYR actually had the better of it, 0.70 expected goals to 0.52, and trailed only because Evan Rodrigues scored on a 5 percent chance with 30 seconds left. Then the second period turned it into a blowout. NJD out-chanced NYR 1.16 to 0.23 in expected goals and scored four times, three of them in a span of about four and a half minutes. Luke Hughes opened it 18 seconds in, Nico Hischier and Arseny Gritsyuk added goals at 4:08 and 4:39, and Hughes scored again at 16:34.

Some of that was finishing luck. Hughes' first goal came on a 2 percent chance, and Gritsyuk's on a 3 percent chance. Dylan Garand allowed 3.0 goals more than his 13 shots against deserved, giving up four before Spencer Martin took over and stopped 15 of 18. Nico Daws made 18 saves on 19 shots, 0.78 goals better than expected, which included stopping Oliver Bjorkstrand on a 26 percent look in the third.

The play still backed up the lead. NJD finished with 3.05 expected goals to 1.78 and 69 shot attempts to 43, and won 72 percent of simulated replays. At even strength the gap was wider, 2.38 to 0.82. Stefan Noesen made it 6-0 at 7:01 of the third, Pavel Dorofeyev answered on the power play, and Cody Glass scored shorthanded at 14:54. NJD went 0 for 4 on its own power plays and still won by six.
